The Gemara rejects it as proof - it may refer only to that verse and things like it, not to every prohibition that warrants lashes.
reason: l01b: 'come and hear from that which was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says: for any sin from You shall not take the name...and below, repentance atones' - exact, dominant match.

stepLabel: The reed dispute over immersion-at-its-time
stepText: In that baraita the Rabbis and Rabbi Yosei disagree precisely over tevila bizmanah. The Rabbis say immersion at its proper time is not a mitzva, so without a reed one waits even until the next day rather than risk erasing the name. Rabbi Yosei says it is a mitzva, so one immerses at the proper time even without covering the name - the opposite of the inference drawn above.
reason: l19a: 'we maintain that they disagree as to whether or not immersion at its proper time is a mitzva. According to the Rabbis, immersion at its proper time is not a mitzva...' - exact, dominant match.

stepLabel: Reattributing the baraita to Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda
stepText: The resolution: the 'Rabbi Yosei' of that reed baraita is actually Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, who taught 'it suffices that the immersion be at the end' - one need only immerse once when surely pure, not repeatedly to hit the exact proper time. So he too holds immersion-at-its-time is not a binding mitzva, removing the contradiction.
reason: l19b: 'this Rabbi Yosei mentioned in the baraita is actually Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda...Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: it is sufficient for the immersion to be at the end' - exact, dominant match.
